weekend trip to chiapas san cristobal sumidero wall of text i live less than an hour from the san diego tijuana crossborder express bridge and i finally took an opportunity to use it to explore a bit of mexican hinterland the original plan was cross cbx early in the morning on friday and fly to tuxtla then somehow get to san cristobal take a fullday tour of sumidero canyon on saturday look around the city some more on sunday morning then fly back landing in tijuana at 6 pm on sunday i paid 363 for the flight seat upgrades 158 for two nights in a hotel 52 for the tour and 55 for the cbx 628 total before travel expenses restaurants etc friday i got to cbx at 550 on friday for the 750 am flight the walk across the border was fairly quick except for the 20 minute wait in line for the immigration authorities i was at the gate with tons of time to spare i brought 300 usd in cash which i ended up not needing at all and i exchanged another 100 for 1700 mxn in the airport which i ended up spending entirely the airline viva turned out to be the most budget barebones of any airlines i ever flew on not only was carryon luggage extra the allowance was only for a single personal item such as a backpack up to 10 kg but there was no wifi at all not even for purchase and all snacks and drinks were extra i never got to find out how much extra because on all legs of my flights the menu was missing from the pockets in front of my seats i started to get apprehensive when the plane was still on the ground 30 minutes after the scheduled departure time the plane was scheduled to arrive at 1245 we actually touched down around 105 and then spent a loooong time taxiing or just standing near the terminal i was near the front row 9 and i rushed for the connecting gate as soon as i could which was around 125 the flight to tuxtla was scheduled to leave at 140 and of course it was at the opposite end of the terminal but i figured that the airline knew i was connecting and the plane could wait a couple minutes at the gate the sign read last call the gate itself was closed and there was an airline attendant and two or three other passengers waiting the attendant checked my boarding pass and asked us all to follow i did unsure where we were going we walked all the way back to the gate i arrived from then to baggage claim and finally to the viva counter in front of the airport between her explanations and info from flight apps i eventually learned that my flight for tuxtla actually left at 133 the airline was going to send me there some other way they had two possible routes through monterrey or through mexico city but in either case the earliest i could get to tuxtla was saturday afternoon almost 24 hours late at this point i considered just aborting the whole thing but decided to move the itinerary back one day i got a hotel room in holiday inn guadalajara airport messaged the hotel in san cristobal booked a new tour of sumidero for sunday instead of saturday and set about figuring out how to get to the hotel the front of guadalajara airport was a zoo i tried to get an uber but gave up when the driver started interrogating me about something over the phone in spanish i got the impression possibly incorrect that he was saying he could not drive into the airport and was asking where to meet me instead i went back inside found the taxis counter and they sold me a ticket 310 mxn which i gave to the driver of one of the official taxis a short drive could have been shorter if not for the stopandgo traffic and massive construction and i was in holiday inn here i was on a more secure ground this was a perfectly conventional hotel and the front desk lady spoke english i asked for a shuttle to the airport for 5 am got to my room and turned in saturday next morning i was up early for once everything went smoothly i was out of the hotel at 5 onboard the plane at 530 and walking off the plane in mexico city just as the sun was rising at 7 the nlu airport is very new half of the retail spaces are still vacant i wandered up and down the terminal for a time ate breakfast in a taqueria then dropped in to a lounge just to see what its like turned out that the lounge had a small free buffet and free coffee and at 11 was in line to board the next flight at 115 i was on the ground in chiapas the next stage was the source of some uncertainty i was not clear how to get from the airport to san cristobal fortunately it proved to be easy i simply followed the signs for colectivo paid 300 mxn and was directed to a waiting area and then to a microbus there were around 20 seats on the bus and all were taken by 3 pm i finally reached san cristobal the bus dropped everyone off a few blocks from the center and i walked to the hotel the city makes a generally favorable impression the center is wellkept and has several pedestrianonly streets lined with shops and restaurants it strongly reminded me of antigua guatemala which i visited twice before same narrow cobbled oneway streets narrow sidewalks one or occasionally twostory buildings and at least three cathedrals within five blocks from the central plaza like more or less everywhere outside the us there is some problem with graffiti but they manage to keep it out of the center beyond the central district its more hitandmiss with varying levels of scruff and neglect there were lots of people around most were apparently locals or at least mexicans a side note one thing not immediately apparent from the map is that tuxtlachiapasumidero are in the lowlands but san cristobal is quite high up in the mountains in fact it is at the altitude of 7000 ft for californians same altitude as say mammoth lakes as such it is significantly cooler than tuxtla in january despite its tropical latitude air temperature drops into the 50s after sunset and into the 40s at night i was registered at casa santa lucia though advertised as a hotel in reality and probably like 80 of hotels in the central district it is probably best classified as a bb it is essentially a twostory spanishcolonial style house with a central atrium and rooms around it by my count they have no more than 8 or 9 rooms the place was nice though the room was not impersonal it was very pleasantly appointed and decorated the only oddities were that the window in the room opened onto the atrium and the dining area and i had to ring the doorbell every time i went in or out because the lobby such as it was was always kept locked i unpacked went for a walk found a place to eat dinner and had an early night sunday the tour group met in front of a cafe on the central plaza around 20 people showed up some were localmexican but probably half were clearly foreign tourists there were people from the us from canada and even one woman from germany we were shepherded into two microbuses and the buses set off down the mountain first we visited two vista points along the rim of the canyon at the second point there was an openair restaurant and a few tables with vendors and we spent half an hour there then the buses went north out of the city to a riverside town by the hydroelectric dam we all transferred into boats and the second part of the tour up the river began while the buses went back without us the views up from the river are quite stunning i took numerous pictures until my camera battery ran down we spotted countless birds a huge iguana several crocodiles and in one tree several spider monkeys those unfortunately were shy and obscured by vegetation and even with a 400 mm lens i did not manage to make any decent shots the only downside was the rather depressing amount of floating trash in the river it was concentrated mostly downstream near our starting area and uneven areas of mostly clear surface interspersed with patches of garbage mostly empty plastic bottles and a nontrivial number of shoes we were told that they try to clean the river but the government does not have enough money the guide also said that it gets worse during the rainy season i dont even want to imagine what it looks like when its worse we finally landed on the pier in chiapa del corzo at 3 pm and were given an hour to eat explore and shop i was not hungry so i just walked around through 5 blocks of vendors selling essentially identical blouses carvings bracelets magnets i really dont see how this arrangement makes any economic sense in sweltering heat it was easily over 90 f and not a cloud in the sky at this point i finally almost got bitten by my poor spanish the driver of our bus spoke rapid and not always very clear spanish and i was generally lucky to get half of what he was saying there was a notable contrast with the boats pilot whom i understood fairly well i understood him to say that we would meet at 410 right there at the riverfront and only much later almost by accident discovered that it was supposed to be 410 at la pila several blocks away i rushed to the correct spot and managed to reunite with the group monday i had a few hours to kill before heading for the airport i grabbed the camera and headed back into the city north of the central park the sketchiness level notably increased on the nearempty plaza de la paz several people with a banner and a loudspeaker were demanding justice for oscar trinidad carbajal on the north side of the plaza there was a long line of people by the looks of it mostly indigenes just standing and waiting they seemed to be waiting for the bank to open on the streets there were virtually no apparent tourists but lots of locals many of them indigenous women some leading young children or carrying infants on their backs as seems to be the custom here graffiti and occasional beggars reappeared i went two or three blocks before turning back around 10 i finally checked out from the hotel and went to the bus station at the corner of 190 and insurgentes the area there was more akin to the mexico i was used to noise people going in all directions busted up pavement wandering vendors hawking everything from cut fruit to tv remote controls a traffic jam i got a bit overwhelmed and i got talked into paying my last 250 mxn for a colectivo going to the airport at 1130 minutes later i discovered that i was right next to the occado bus terminal which had two buses to the airport listed on the departures screen i cursed my gullibility for well over an hour until i managed to pull up the ado web site on my phone and discover that ado charges 292 mxn for the same trip and likely uses the same microbuses by comparison they only charge 88 mxn to go to tuxtla which is almost the same distance a direct flight took me back to tijuana and by 7 pm pst i was back in the united states conclusions mexico is not all that scary i need to work on my spanish next time bring more cash

i heard the voice of god the first time i heard the voice i was kneeling at the edge of my wifes hospital bed as she took her final rasping breath i almost brushed it off as hallucination but the voice persisted it was less of a voice as it was an emotion a certainty more overpowering than any i have felt before or since it was intoxicating to the mind and i bathed in its sublime and beautiful pleasure it promised such wonderful things the coming of our savior and the great world that awaited us it promised me a place of power in this holy kingdom a place as advisor and prophet and all the voice asked of me was to prove my faith to travel through the bowels of the earth and discover the final hidden testament to its existence and weeks later as i stared down into the abyss into which the voice has instructed me to travel i imagined the splendor and joy that would be delivered to the world after i would return with this sacred knowledge the crew i had gathered sat a few feet off from the cave checking and double checking equipment they examined the sturdiness of the ropes and ensured that our food and water would last us several days they were left unaware of the true purpose of this journey to them this was a hobby a passion project they had jumped at the chance to explore a new subterranean chamber for me this was no mere activity but a pilgrimage i was so lost in my thoughts that i jumped when someone spoke are you sure about this an unmapped cave can be a bit dangerous for someone who hasnt gone caving before i sighed in relief at the sight of the man in front of me the most energetic of the cavers derrick had already made his way into alpha status among the group his laughter seemed to make the others light up with joy i however could not take part in these trivial joys i had tasted of the voice of god and nothing in this realm could possibly compare to the bliss i have felt when it spoke i nodded sharply in answer to his question irritated by his words of course i was sure about this not only was my place in the promised land at stake but the holy transcendence of humanity as well derrick gave me a concerned glance as if he could see through my stoic visage eventually he merely shrugged and called out okay well were about to have dinner if you want to come sit by the fire with us i nearly ignored him and returned to examining the cave as i hadnt felt hunger in the weeks leading up to the trip the voice had sustained me more than any food possibly could but the voice spoke in the back of my mind instructing me to join the group observe the last actions you will see of a primal race i nodded zealously and derrick smiled he thought he was getting through to me turning me into another one of his followers but my only master is the voice i walked towards the fire the heat a jarring transition from the cool cave air i sat down on a rock next to robert the oldest of the cavers he patted my back roughly and i somehow managed to avoid strangling him good to see you up and moving i had half a mind to go check and see if you had died over there robert broke into hearty laughter meaty hands pounding the ground beside him and kicking up a small cloud of dust leave the poor man alone hes been over here for two seconds and he already thinks were crazy derrick said with a smile the rest of the group laughed as robert passed out the meals arent you going to eat asked sam resting her head in her hands blue eyes sparkling in the firelight the cavers had already finished their meals but i had taken one bite and recoiled the curse of fey food had nothing on the blessings of the lord not hungry i replied quietly as everyone finished packing up okay i guess well be heading into the cave then she said handing me the rope that she had already tied to her waist i attached the thin coil of rope to my harness and we climbed down the first drop into the chasm below as the light grew weaker to the point that our lanterns only exposed a few feet in front of us i was rejuvenated by a feeling of ecstasy the darkness was pure destroying any semblance of unholy light the word still sickens me to this moment and the actual presence of it drives me into agony i was shaken out of thought by derrick crudely interrupting the sweet silence of the cavern everyone stay close and if anyone needs to stop pull on the line the voice was a harsh grating scraping nails on a chalkboard sound a defilement of the silent divinity around us i jumped back disgusted to be chained to this vile blasphemer are you okay back there man derrick called back to me hastily i thought of a reply im fine thought i brushed something okay he replied suddenly suspicious i regretted my actions immediately silently begging for forgiveness for my transgressions you may be forgiven now is the time to prove yourself in front of you is a tunnel heading left head down this path and reach your destiny the voice was more powerful this deep into the cave a euphoria so strong it was almost agonizing a faint gasp escaped my lips as i was flooded with a feeling no man could comprehend other than one who has heard the voice i stopped walking and sam nearly fell as the rope went taut hey whyd you stop sam hollered at me you almost broke my neck and good riddance that would be i spat in reply curling my hands into fists sam flinched back and i grinned in triumph is this what life would feel like after i had found the testament the power of her fear filled me almost as pleasing as the voices tones but i could not get distracted by such trivial things not yet okay you two lets just calm down and keep going im sure it was an accident right derrick stepped between the two of us concern showing on his face as he turned to me i saw my chance we need to keep going theres a tunnel to the left of us and we need to go that way youre not changing the subject youre going to apologize to sam and then well decide what were doing derrick said who did he think he was to treat me like a child being punished i was gods chosen messenger i would not be talked down on in such a way i pulled out my pocket knife and flicked it open i raised it above my head before furiously slicing down on the thick rope severing myself off from the rest of the group silently i brush past the group and head deeper into the caverns derrick didnt merely yell for me to come back but lunged onto my body he was strong from the years of caving but the voice was stronger as rage surged through me i slammed my head backwards into his jaw throwing him off me i quickly sprinted into the darkness they werent so foolish to come after if they would not follow me to the tunnel they no longer served my purpose i was glad to leave them behind i headed down the damp gloriously cold tunnel my eyes slowly adjusted to the pitch darkness and i saw beautiful structures of stone from huge monoliths to almost sculpturesque monuments even i could not help but gawk at the majesty of the underground only a god could create such beauty gaze upon it and wonder the shaft went on for what felt like an eternity as i gazed upon the rocks which almost resembled the bodies of man i barely noticed as it grew narrower and narrower guiding me towards what i was predestined to see eventually i had to stand with my body turned so that i was able to continue forward i am surprised to see no offshoot passages as there were many at the entrance to the ancient cave system i nearly ran into the cavern wall as the tunnel veered sharply left my eyes widened in excitement i was almost there i had almost delivered man into the benevolent hands of god how they would all thank me once they too could see the beauty of this place i saw a glow at the end of the tunnel but not something so simple as a man made light no this was darker holier although the cave was black as tar and any mere man would not be able to see at all the light is somehow even more shadowed a void within space a darkness so sanctified my eyes burned with pleasure as i gazed upon it i attempted to rush towards the glow knowing this was what i had come miles to view but at this point the cavern was so narrow i nearly got stuck unable to push forward the agony of being so close and yet so horribly far away was torturous and i cried out the voice urged me forward and i forced through the darkness rocks scraping muscle and tendon as i reached the light i saw that it was a large black crystalline heart the heart pulsed and throbbed and each time it did so i felt the same joyful exaltation the voice provides me this is the strongest i had ever felt it and it is so powerful it felt as if it was trying to bust out of my skull this rapture was sharp and powerful a sword of fire in my brain i stuck my hand out reaching for the heart as i touched it the veil was lifted from my eyes and a vignette of images passed through my mind the corpses of my crew horribly transmogrified in stone the world in flames a blackened figure watching over it all and finally the mountain rising up from its resting place revealing a horrible cyclopian creature i finally understood the deity i have been serving the cruel mockery of man that i called savior the twisted and evil stone beneath the earth it has no plans to aid humanity but to devour them make them a small meaningless piece of this god and the worst part of its loathsome plans is that it believes everything that it whispered in my ear at night every promise every word of its horrible indescribable wrongness it thinks is true i grasped my face in horror and forced myself deeper into the cave the world did not deserve me for my vile sins against all of mankind i shoved through the horrid darkness knowing that any escape from it would blind me my bones cracked under the pressure of the earth around me but i kept going determined to distance myself from the beating of its atrocious heart my life up to this point has been meaningless my only goal to serve a being bent on the destruction of humanity my god has failed me and i have failed mankind and as i carve this into the stone with a rock broken off one of my fallen companions i know this warning will be the only thing i have provided this world that will ever matter even now i can feel my limbs growing heavy and my feet are planted permanently on this ground that i have grown to despise i cannot escape my fate and i have accepted my end but i will get out my story before i fall to this cruel death this is my final testament and this is the beginning of the end

ai video evolves from static clips to realtime simulations indie dev here whos been tinkering with simulations for a while came across this realtime generative thing called pixverse r1 and honestly its kinda different from the usual ai video stuff so while most ai video tools you prompt something and it renders a clip from scratch this one actually builds frame by frame in real time everything prompts frames audio goes through one transformer trained on tons of real world footage the interesting bit is it seems to learn actual physics from seeing how objects move in all that training data uses autoregressive memory so each frame builds on the last one means if something happens early on it actually persists later which is not something ive seen work well before like their demo has a 10min fantasy fight where stuff that breaks stays broken they cut denoising steps from 50 down to 4ish which is how its rendering multi character scenes in seconds the difference vs runwayveoetc is those make pretty clips but each one is isolated this tries to make continuous simulations instead what im wondering is could this actually enable stuff we couldnt do before like what if you could generate a whole procedural game level that responds to player actions in real time or those chooseyourownadventure interactive shows but actually generated on the fly based on your choices imagine walking through a virtual space where the environment generates around you as you move instead of being prerendered hell what about first person experiences where the ai maintains your pov through a whole scenario like training simulations or even just exploring fantasy worlds from your perspective it still breaks down after running too long but im curious if anyone has thoughts on what happens when you can generate persistent simulated environments instead of just clips feels like the constraint has always been make a cool 10sec video but what changes when its simulate an ongoing scenario are we looking at actual realtime metaverse type stuff or am i just overhyping another demo

what its actually like at bitsdes long vent post created this post because i just wanted somewhere to put all my thoughts about bitsdes and what its like to be a student here again this is both a vent post and an informational post so its likely to be a bit jumbled bear with it other current students feel free to correct me on factual errors location located in pawshepada near kalyan bits mumbai is nowhere near mumbai there is a dmart 3 kms away along with a zudio theobroma et cetera and you can get autos outside the college who will charge you either 4050 per person or 200300 according to their mood to take you there on the other side there are a few temples ulhaas river and lots of greenery and potential trekking areas takes over three hours to reach via cab from the airports and is 20 minutes away from shahad local station and 45 minutes away from kalyan station common mode of transport when we go out to the city is taking a local train from shahad we mostly only take autos when going to cosplay events or travelling with cameras selection process and scholarships genuinely have no idea about this one but its a question thats asked a lot so the college says they cant give a proper ranking list of people they take because its based off of a bunch of combined factors such as their entrance exam score uceednidbitsdatwhatever else and their interview and portfolio score and that the scholarship is based off of this so in the eyes of those that dont have a scholarship this is not justified properly and you could simply call me salty for not being one of the people with scholarship but i dont like that even if someone who had a scholarship lost one no one else gets one also scholarships arent evaluated or reevaluated based on your performance in college which is where everyone starts on fair groundno i dont need to be told thats how it is i know online shopping and deliveries amazon flipkart myntra meesho et cetera all deliver here but expect it to take 25 weeks for the parcel to arrive even with prime and equivalent services zepto delivers blinkit doesnt dont know about zomato swiggy delivers but delivery rates are high curfew and related freedom campus out curfew is 530 am and in curfew in 10 pm if you return later than 10 pm a warning is issued the warden will yell at you and your parents are informed emailed i think hostel in curfew is 2 am and out curfew is same as gate in theory to leave campus currently you need to apply 30 minutes prior for an outpass through an app and then leave through the facerecognition based flap thats at the gate your parents get an email every time you leave long leaves overnight leaves and such are also applied for through the same app and need to be approved by parents they get an automatic call that asks them to press a number to agree or deny hostels currently there are three hostel buildings being used h1 is used by bitsom pg students on a singlesharing basis h2 is used by a mix of law and design ug students on a doublesharing basis first years get randomly allotted roommates of the same gender from the same course and batch and second years and upwards can mutually choose their roommates while other bits campuses allot single rooms from third year onwards even for ug currently there seem to be no plans for that on this campus as law third years also have doublesharing rooms two more hostels are set to be completed by the end of this academic year aprmay so that might change but as of now theres no confirmation on that each doublesharing hostel room contains one bunk bed two closets one desk with two drawers two wall shelves above each desk four in total a bedside table with one open shelf and one drawer for each bed two open shelves and two drawers in total and an attached bathroom with a geyser and the usual amenities each hostel has at least one water filter per floor i hope as far as i know that supplies room temp cold water on the ground floor there are two common fridges in the reception area two microwaves veg and non veg one water filter with cold room temp and hot water and one electric kettle electric kettles are prohibited in rooms the hostel has two common rooms that seat with difficulty about 20 people each each has adequate halfbroken office chairs and about 5 square wooden tables due to circumstances and increasing use a few pockets of space outside these on the ground floor have also been filled with tables and chairs academic block which is about a 78 minute walk from hostels closes at 12 midnight cutting off access to whiteboards and pinboards while making it an unpreferred option for working at as most modules give group projects and most of these projects extend beyond 12 after 12 that leaves the cafeteria and hostel common rooms to work at with cafeteria having minimal plug points and closing at 2 am and hostel being a quiet space where any slightly loud discussion gets you yelled at laundry there are a few paid 80100 rs based on temperature of wash washing machines scattered across the hostel floors think like 3 per hostel divided between girls and guys floors and they dont have driers the room has no drying space and no overhead fan so drying anything there is your fun problem to solve the bathroom has extendable drying lines but no ventilation of its own so anything takes days to dry there and you just gotta hope it doesnt catch mold by then they give you drying stands to put in your room if you want but good luck finding space for it there is a laundromat on campus and you get 40 pieces of laundry free per month you give them the clothes and get them back in one day for wash and two days for washiron anything beyond 40 is paid i dont know how much because ive never crossed that i just wash in the machines they also do paid drycleaning cleaning of shoes soft toys mats blankets et cetera currently irons are prohibited in the hostel and there is no common iron so in theory your only option if you repairs and maintenance repairs and room cleaning are applied for through an app and response is usually delayed even for things marked as an emergency mold problems caused due to poor ventilation in rooms can be requested to be cleaned though how long it takes them to respond varies based on their mood ant infestations affecting multiple rooms were not dealt with for days with cleaning staff arriving after ants had left and advising students to get repellent if they bothered them again on multiple occasions repair staff arrive after 10 pm at which point they are told they arent allowed to subject to change until the last minute with no one person taking initiative to provide clarity any faults pointed out are turned back on the students to point out their selfishness or inadequacy administration of the design course seems severely understaffed and overworked and administration of the college campus seems severely out of touch with student problems and campus life or lack store to get and there are no stationery stores nearby except dmart wood metal ceramic labs acquire material for courses and any leftover material can be used for exploration probably its being done the 20minute experiment that predicted your last breakup relationship intelligence rq i used to think relationship problems were mysterious like some cosmic lottery where you either got lucky or you didnt then i learned about mary ainsworths strange situation in the 1970s ainsworth did something simple she put oneyearolds in a room with their mothers then she had the mothers leave then come back thats it twenty minutes one room a few toys what she found was insane the pattern that repeats forever ainsworth watched how babies responded when their mothers left the room some cried but calmed down quickly when mom returned others avoided eye contact entirely some couldnt be soothed at all the wild part those same patterns showed up 22 years later in their romantic relationships the kid who turned away from mom at 18 months still turning away from partners in their twenties the one who couldnt be comforted still inconsolable during conflict decades later heres what everyone gets wrong about this research people think its about childhood trauma or bad parenting nope its about invisible behavioral patterns that repeat across every relationship youll ever have the three patterns youre living out right now ainsworth identified three attachment styles not personality types not diagnoses observable behavioral patterns secure attachment showed up in 65 of the babies globally these kids used their mothers as a safe base they explored the room when mom left they got upset when she returned they sought comfort and then went back to playing translation to your adult life you can handle conflict you express needs directly you dont spiral when your partner needs space avoidant attachment appeared in 21 of babies these kids didnt cry when mom left they actively avoided her when she came back they looked away moved to a different part of the room but heres the key insight from ainsworths narrative records these babies werent indifferent they had learned that showing emotional needs didnt work so they stopped showing them translation to your adult life you shut down during arguments you say youre fine when youre not you leave before someone can leave you anxious attachment showed up in 14 of babies these kids were already anxious before mom left when she returned they couldnt be soothed they wanted comfort but also pushed her away translation to your adult life you need constant reassurance you read into every text delay you create tests to see if your partner really cares why this matters more than you think most relationship advice treats every fight like its unique different topic different solution thats backwards the research shows that what matters is sensitivity not the content of what you say not your communication skills sensitivity means you detect signals from your partner you interpret them correctly you respond in a timely and relevant way the babies who became secure their mothers were sensitive they read the babys cues accurately hungry cry versus tired cry versus scared cry then they responded appropriately the babies who became avoidant their mothers missed signals or dismissed them the baby learned that communicating needs was pointless the babies who became anxious their mothers were inconsistent sometimes responsive sometimes not the baby never knew what to expect the part nobody talks about heres what makes this uncomfortable your attachment style isnt fixed about 3040 of people show different attachment patterns from childhood to adulthood but its also not random if you keep ending up in the same relationship pattern youre probably running the same program i see this constantly someone dates an avoidant person complains about emotional unavailability breaks up then dates another avoidant person acts shocked when the same pattern emerges the pattern isnt the problem the invisibility of the pattern is the problem what this looks like in real relationships let me make this concrete secure people fight differently when conflict happens they move toward their partner they say what they need they listen to what their partner needs they dont catastrophize one fight doesnt mean the relationship is over only 38 of americans report having a secure attachment style that means most relationships have at least one person operating from an insecure pattern avoidant people disappear during conflict not always physically sometimes they just go silent shut down emotionally change the subject say everything is fine when it clearly isnt theyre not trying to be difficult they learned early that emotional expression leads to rejection so they protect themselves by not expressing anything anxious people escalate during conflict they need resolution immediately they cant tolerate ambiguity they interpret silence as abandonment they ask are we okay seventeen times theyre not trying to be clingy they learned early that love is unpredictable so they monitor constantly for signs of withdrawal the worst combination anxious people often pair with avoidant people the anxious person seeks closeness the avoidant person needs space the anxious person interprets the need for space as rejection the avoidant person interprets the pursuit as suffocation both people confirm their worst fears about relationships this isnt bad luck its pattern recognition failure the signal you keep missing most people think they know their attachment style they take a quiz read a description recognize themselves thats not enough knowing your pattern intellectually doesnt change your pattern behaviorally you need to see it happening in real time not after the fight not during the postmortem during the actual moment when the pattern activates this is where most relationship advice fails it gives you frameworks to think about after the fact but your attachment pattern doesnt operate at the thinking level it operates at the reaction level when your partner says we need to talk your body responds before your brain does your nervous system makes a prediction based on every previous we need to talk youve ever experienced if those conversations historically led to rejection your system prepares for rejection you shut down or flee or pick a fight first if those conversations historically led to resolution your system stays calm you can actually listen what actually changes patterns heres what ive learned from building a tool that measures this stuff change doesnt come from understanding your attachment style change comes from seeing your pattern activate in real time and choosing a different response that requires three things first you need visibility you cant change what you cant see most people only notice their pattern after the damage is done you need to catch it earlier when your voice changes when your body tenses when you start planning your exit strategy midconversation second you need neutrality your partner cant give you this feedback theyre too invested theyre running their own pattern you need an external observation layer that doesnt have a stake in the outcome third you need repetition one insight doesnt rewire decades of behavioral programming you need to see the pattern activate interrupt it and choose differently hundreds of times this is why therapy works when it works not because of the insights because youre practicing a different response pattern with someone who stays regulated when you dont the part about voice ainsworth noticed something specific in her observations babies didnt just behave differently they sounded different secure babies had cries that communicated clear needs avoidant babies had flat affect anxious babies had escalating hardtosoothe vocalizations those vocal patterns persist into adulthood when youre activated your voice changes pitch shifts pace changes tone flattens or sharpens these changes happen before youre consciously aware youre activated your partner hears it they respond to it usually by activating their own pattern then youre both running programs instead of having a conversation this is the signal most people miss youre focused on the words the actual information is in how youre saying them stop doing this stop treating every relationship problem like its a new problem if you keep ending up in the same place with different people you have a pattern problem not a partner selection problem stop thinking awareness alone will change your behavior knowing youre avoidant doesnt make you less avoidant in the moment you need realtime feedback when the pattern activates stop waiting for the right person to fix your attachment issues secure people dont fix insecure people they just tolerate the pattern better or they dont then youre single again running the same program what to do instead start tracking your pattern in real time not after the fight during it notice when your body changes during conversations when you want to leave when you go silent when you need immediate reassurance thats your pattern activating get external observation record your conversations if your partner agrees listen back youll hear things you didnt notice in the moment tone shifts defensive patterns escalation triggers practice different responses when youre not activated you cant learn a new pattern in the middle of a fight you need to rehearse the alternative when your nervous system is calm find relationships where you can practice security not just romantic ones friendships work relationships any context where you can experience consistent responsive interaction the research shows that patterns can change but change requires more than insight it requires repeated experience of a different outcome the real work ainsworths strange situation wasnt just about babies it was about showing that relationship patterns are observable measurable and predictable youre not mysteriously incompatible with everyone you date youre running a program that program made sense when you developed it it kept you safe when you were small and dependent but its probably not serving you now the good news patterns that were learned can be unlearned not through understanding through different experience repeated enough times that your nervous system updates its predictions most people never do this work they just keep dating different versions of the same person having different versions of the same fight wondering why relationships feel so hard the pattern will keep repeating until you make it visible start paying attention to your signals the ones you send the ones you miss the ones you misinterpret thats where change actually happens create your relationship intelligence rq encountrai

challenger space shuttle disaster shocks nation in 1986 on january 28 1986 the space shuttle challenger broke apart just 73 seconds after liftoff from kennedy space center in florida killing all seven astronauts on board among them was christa mcauliffe a new hampshire teacher selected for nasas teacher in space program whose presence had brought unprecedented public attention to the mission the explosion unfolded live on television abruptly halting what had been promoted as a routine launch and confronting the nation with the inherent dangers of human spaceflight the shuttle disintegrated after a failure in the solid rocket booster orings which lost their ability to seal in unusually cold launch conditions engineers had raised concerns about launching in low temperatures but those warnings did not ultimately prevent the mission from proceeding the accident exposed deeper organizational problems within nasa including communication breakdowns schedule pressure and what investigators later described as a normalization of known technical risks in response president ronald reagan appointed the rogers commission to investigate the disaster the commissions findings went beyond the immediate mechanical failure identifying flaws in nasas decisionmaking culture and safety oversight as a result the space shuttle program was grounded for nearly three years the booster design was modified and nasa implemented sweeping changes to its safety protocols management structure and launch approval process the challenger disaster marked a turning point in how americans viewed the us space program it tempered public optimism with a more sober understanding of risk and accountability reshaped how crewed missions were communicated to the public and influenced safety practices for future programs including the international space station and later human spaceflight initiatives how do you think the challenger disaster continues to shape public trust and expectations around space exploration today

using chatgpt for app ideas i find this trend genuinely funny a lot of people now go to chatgpt to brainstorm a startup idea vibecode it ship in 10 to 30 days and then discover there are already 10 to 35 nearidentical apps with identical color themes design and features sitting in the apple app store this is not because chatgpt failed them it is because many people misunderstand what llms actually do chatgpt does not generate new ideas in the human sense it learns from existing data and predicts the most likely next output based on your prompt you can think of it as a very advanced calculator for probability when you ask it for an app idea it naturally converges toward ideas that many others have already explored that is why the ideas feel familiar that is also why the space feels crowded so quickly do not get discouraged chatgpt is an excellent tool for brainstorming and execution just do not take the first idea it gives you or even the twentieth be creative pay attention to what you care about what annoys you and what genuinely excites you then use chatgpt to help you build something that could truly resonate with people like you

turning business setbacks into legacy if youve ever dreamed of building something meaningful if youve ever faced the fear of failure and wondered whether to keep going this message is for you at thrive we believe that every setback is a setup for an incredible comeback today were exploring the powerful stories of some of the worlds greatest entrepreneurs and how they turned near bankruptcy into brilliance success stories often shine brightly in business magazines and social media feeds but what lies behind those headlines is often years of hardship near failure and moments when everything could have collapsed entrepreneurship is not a straight line to riches and recognition it is a winding and often treacherous path filled with obstacles cashflow crises bad decisions and external shocks that can bring even the most promising ventures to their knees yet time and again we find that some of the worlds most successful entrepreneurs faced moments when bankruptcy loomed large over them only to claw their way back to the top today i want to take you on a journey through the stories of men and women who were at the brink of losing everything and yet managed to stage remarkable comebacks their turnarounds reveal strategies mindset shifts and unconventional decisions that anyone can learn from take walt disney today disney is synonymous with magic creativity and global influence but rewind to 1923 and you find a young walt disney in kansas city watching his first animation studio collapse under financial pressure at the time he had been producing short animated fairy tales but poor management and bad distribution deals led to bankruptcy he was left with a suitcase some drawing tools and barely enough money to get by most people would have abandoned the dream right then but disney saw opportunity in failure instead of creating animations for hire he realized he needed to own his characters that shift in thinking transformed his trajectory when disney created mickey mouse in 1928 he built more than a cartoon he built intellectual property he could control merchandise and expand ownership meant that each new cartoon wasnt just a paycheck it was an asset that could multiply in value over decades disneys persistence was legendary he pitched mickey to dozens of distributors facing constant rejection many thought audiences wouldnt accept a talking mouse but walts conviction carried him through every closed door that combination of assetbuilding and resilience became the cornerstone of the disney empire his story shows that survival sometimes means not just working harder but working smarter shifting from onetime transactions to building assets that create lasting value now lets turn to steve jobs his name is tied forever to apples meteoric success but few remember that in 1985 jobs was fired from the very company he cofounded at just 30 years old his reputation was shattered his wealth was tied up in plummeting apple stock and his career seemed uncertain he started next a new computer company but its high price tag made it a commercial flop by the late 1980s many believed jobs best days were behind him but jobs didnt stop building while next bled money he poured his energy into pixar a struggling animation studio he held on through years of losses believing in the potential of computergenerated films in 1995 pixar released toy story the worlds first fully computeranimated feature film and the gamble paid off pixar went public and jobs became a billionaire again even more remarkable failure at next became the seed of apples rebirth in 1997 apple desperate for innovation bought next for 429 million that acquisition brought jobs back along with nexts advanced software which became the foundation for macos within a decade jobs would lead apple to launch the ipod the iphone and the ipad revolutionizing entire industries his comeback was rooted in vision and diversification jobs never abandoned his obsession with design and user experience but he also knew not to rely on one venture alone pixar was his lifeline his ability to keep investing in longterm vision rather than chasing shortterm wins saved him elon musk offers another powerful case study after selling paypal in 2002 for 180 million musk could have retired comfortably instead he put nearly all his fortune into three companies tesla spacex and solarcity by 2008 this boldness nearly destroyed him the global financial crisis made raising money almost impossible tesla was weeks away from bankruptcy spacex had failed its first three rocket launches musk himself admitted he was borrowing money from friends just to pay rent what turned things around first relentless fundraising musk pitched investors again and again finally securing 40 million in emergency funding to keep tesla alive second sheer resilience most entrepreneurs would have quit after three failed launches but musk refused to stop on spacexs fourth attempt the falcon 1 reached orbit successfully that single success changed everything winning spacex a 16 billion contract with nasa within months tesla also secured a 465 million loan from the us department of energy from the brink of collapse musks companies surged forward his story proves that sometimes survival isnt about clever strategy but pure endurance musks mission to accelerate sustainable energy and make humanity multiplanetary kept him going when the numbers didnt in business especially when facing bankruptcy resilience itself becomes the greatest strategy consider oprah winfreys journey today shes one of the wealthiest women in the world but early in her career she faced humiliation and hardship as a young television anchor in baltimore she was fired and told she wasnt fit for television at the same time she was struggling financially and emotionally unsure where her career would go many would have walked away but oprah leaned into her strengths she realized her gift was not in delivering stiff news reports but in connecting deeply with people when she shifted into daytime talk shows she turned her authenticity into her greatest asset viewers resonated with her openness and empathy the oprah winfrey show became a cultural phenomenon not because it followed the rules but because it broke them but her turnaround was about more than talent it was about ownership oprah negotiated for ownership of her show instead of being just a hired host that one decision created generational wealth and creative freedom her story shows that authenticity and ownership can transform your lowest point into lasting success richard bransons virgin group tells a similar story of resilience in the early 1980s virgin atlantic nearly collapsed under fierce competition and cashflow issues branson made one of the hardest decisions of his life he sold virgin records the company that launched his career to save the airline the sale brought in nearly a billion dollars which he funneled directly into virgin atlantic it was painful but it preserved the brand and kept the dream alive branson doubled down on customer loyalty branding virgin atlantic as fun edgy and customerfirst that identity helped it compete with giants the lesson is sacrifice and focus sometimes to save the dream you must let go of something precious across these stories disney jobs musk oprah branson patterns emerge the first is resilience bankruptcy is not just a financial crisis its an emotional one each of these entrepreneurs endured rejection and loss yet they refused to stop the second is strategic shifts disney moved from service work to intellectual property jobs turned failure into foundation musk mixed mission with relentless funding oprah secured ownership branson sacrificed one asset to save another their turnarounds were not luck they were deliberate pivots built on clarity and courage another key theme is ownership when you own your ideas and your output you hold the power to rebuild ownership gives control when the world falls apart finally each story is driven by vision disney believed in magic jobs in design musk in humanitys future oprah in authenticity branson in rebellion vision gave them courage to act when the numbers screamed quit if you are listening to this and facing your own crisis maybe your business is collapsing debt is mounting or investors are pulling out take heart bankruptcy doesnt have to be the end for many great entrepreneurs it was the turning point the question is not whether you can avoid struggle but how you respond when it comes will you make the sacrifice that saves the dream will you build assets that last will you persist after failure the turnaround stories of disney jobs musk oprah and branson are not fairy tales they are blueprints they remind us that bankruptcy is not failure unless you stop true failure is giving up on the vision that drives you every setback can be the setup for a stronger comeback if you are willing to persist pivot and protect what matters most so the next time your business feels like its teetering on the edge remember this the greatest entrepreneurs in cyberpunk review bonanza system override neon dragons neon dust aura overload and maybe more get your fix here soooo ive been on a bit of cyberpunk binge recently and i figured id put fiveish of the most recent stories down into short reviews along with my larger list of cyberpunk reviews so lets jump in and ill write em out in the order i read them system override review royalroad this is a fanfic similar in style to ghost in the city except instead of an originalish mc were following alternate david martinez where some fun biotechnical child experiments give him nanites and a useful ai in his head add this on top of the sandy that gloria kleps and david is super op from almost day one the pacing is fast and furious and the story balances davids solo career with his excursions with maines group the romance between him and lucy takes a while to build and their barbing is great and the characters feel fully realised instead of just gameanime caricatures good fun outrun royalroad way slower in pace than system override and its not a fanfic the world and characters are all original and theres an interesting combination of cyberpunk style progression software cyberware with magical pathways shiro isnt too keen at all on exploring these magical systems and explicitly avoids initial perks that would grant those powers but quickly becomes entangled in the games of the various eidolons read powerful spirit yokailike creatures in amongst this shiro is trying to do ten thousand other things including for some reason setting up a base in some insanely unreachable underground lair when she has a perfectly good hidden basement floor in an apartment shes also using the progression is skill based and choosing skill perks is a mix of knowledge download or being trapped in a mental dreamscape until she masters the abilities or starves i think the largest issue i had with outrun was simply how much of a loner shiro is solo mcs are fine but solo mcs that dont form lasting 1arc connections means that theres possibly too much of the story thats just in shiros head neon dragons review royalroad similar pacing slowburn to outrun and a similar skillsperks progression system sera isnt a total lone wolf like shiro she has persistent friends and even family and the character interactions help keep you as a reader engaged for longer like shiro lots of different activities fill seras time and youll spend just as much time making noodles on a dingy floor in her megabuilding as training in a combat gym in fancy upper floors then theres learning to code learning to sneak making friends with nonhuman merchants with too many joints in their limbs surviving her mothers torturelessons learning to juggle you name it 95 of the story is currently set in the same building but the author has said sera will be leaving to do more operatorstyle missions more often in the future fun read with my main gripe being about the verbosity repetition of the writing in a technical sense instead of any large plot or character issues neon dust review royalroad i almost gotta call this one progressionadjacent dualmc story where you follow tony cyberwarestripped operator left to die in the blast and addie blast native whos actually a genius with dust oh dust is magic so theres again two clear progression pathways cyberwaredust tony doesnt really progress or upgrade anything until book three which is where a lot of people might be frustrated as the initial books focus more on surviving the setting and forming a new life instead of a rapid climb back into power like you might find in op mc stories like all of plum parrots works the characters and dialogue are on point the worldbuilding is solid and arcs actually wrap up in fact there are three books out now to make a complete arc and plums waiting to see how ku likes the book before committing to another big arc aura overload review royalroad ah but heres the crux this is another of plums thats just started dropping on rr ive read 27 chappies on patreon and its much faster paced than neon dust or cyber dreams and i find the worldbuilding to be more interesting as well think of your normal cyberpunk but add in the neurodecks altered carbons cortical stack which allows consciousness to jump bodies and a history of royal families and cleans in space vying over the solar system some red rising vibes the mc hector is slotted into a new body after 200 years to find out his entire family was exterminated and he needs vengence the system is more classic litrpg with people hector via his neurodeck having aura systems which give archetypes classes like brawler levels stats and abilities like aura blade etc you increase all of these by spending potentia which you can take off fallen enemies very litrpg but without an omniscient system yay oh the crux right if plum has to split time between two cyberpunk stories or focus on only one at this point id be heavily suggesting to just focus on aura overload curious if anyone else has read both and has thoughts on this to add onto these ones ive reviewed longer ago from last read to first read cybergene blood and steel review royalroad skitterdoc 2077 review spacebattles sufficientvelocity never fade away review spacebattles stray cat strut review amazon audible royalroad changeling review royalroad cyber dreams review amazon audible royalroad ghost in the city review royalroad godclads review royalroad anyway thats probably it for six months at least from me on cyberpunk stories unless that is someone is able to suggest some absolute gems ive missed which i need to read

the diagnosed other from relationships that would require tolerating ambiguity and imperfection they become a diagnostician of everyone they meet scanning for red flags interpreting ordinary human behavior as pathological trusting no one fully because anyone might be revealed as the enemy the system that claims to heal creates division the vocabulary of mental health becomes the grammar of exile what remains the human being remains behind the diagnosis beneath the label despite the category a person is there someone who adapted to circumstances they did not choose someone whose difficulties make sense when you understand their origin someone who is more than any clinical term can capture someone who contains multitudes including both the capacity to wound and the capacity to love the woman they call borderline is someone who learned that love was dangerous and unpredictable and still reaches for it desperately imperfectly her intensity is not disease it is the fire of someone who felt too much in an environment that could not hold her given the right conditions relationship attunement patience that fire becomes warmth rather than destruction the man they call narcissist is someone who learned that vulnerability meant annihilation so he built walls his armor is not evil it is architecture constructed when there was no other way to survive behind it if anyone cares to look is often a shame so profound it cannot be faced directly given safety real safety which is rare even that armor can soften both carry wounds both cause harm both deserve to be seen as human both can heal not quickly not easily not without skilled help and genuine relationship and the willingness to feel what has never been felt but the change that the narcissismindustrial complex says is impossible happens every day quietly in therapists offices in relationships where someone chose to stay and work in the slow accumulation of experiences that contradict the old adaptations the witch hunt ended when communities stopped believing in witches the diagnostic hunt will end when we stop believing that labels explain people when we recover the willingness to see each other whole wounded and wounding capable of harm and capable of growth deserving of boundaries and deserving of compassion the person who hurt you was probably hurt themselves this does not make what they did acceptable it makes them human and it opens a possibility that the diagnostic framework forecloses that understanding might coexist with boundaries that compassion might coexist with selfprotection that we might hold someone accountable without casting them out of the human community entirely the diagnostic machine offers moral clarity here are the monsters here are the victims here is the line between them reality offers something more difficult and more true humans hurting humans hurting humans all the way down an unbroken chain of wound passing to wound generation to generation until someone finds the courage to feel what was never felt grieve what was never grieved and break the transmission that someone could be you not by becoming a perfect victim not by identifying all the narcissists and cutting them out but by doing the harder thing metabolizing your own pain so thoroughly that you no longer need to pass it on the torch is in your hands you can keep burning or you can set it down the fire waits for your decision it was always waiting it is still waiting waiting to see what you will choose the moonth what they buried
